note: A job that is part-way through work shows GREEN on the Work Orders list and ORANGE in the search. And inside the search four different stages of a job - Ready for Review, In Progress, Complete and Declined - are all the same orange, so a person cannot tell them apart at a glance, while the Work Orders list does keep In Progress visibly separate.
evidence:
MEASURED 17 SEPTEMBER 2026 on build v26.36.7-29ca209, by reading the colour the product itself applies rather than judging shades by eye. Same signed-in person, the same customer's jobs, the two screens one after the other.

SEARCH RESULTS:
  Ready for Review  orange   background 255,250,235   text 181,71,8
  In Progress       orange   background 255,250,235   text 181,71,8
  Complete          orange   background 255,250,235   text 181,71,8
  Declined          orange   background 255,250,235   text 181,71,8
  Approved          green    background 236,253,243
  Estimate          blue     background 233,245,255
  Invoiced          grey     background 238,242,246

WORK ORDERS LIST:
  In Progress       GREEN    background 217,251,208   text 81,102,62
  Ready for Review  orange   background 255,239,202   text 188,56,3
  Complete          orange   background 255,239,202
  Approved          green    background 224,242,241
  Estimate          blue     background 229,237,255
  Paid              green    background 224,242,241

TWO THINGS FOLLOW. First, In Progress changes colour family between the two screens - green on the list, orange in the search. Second, the search collapses four stages into one colour where the list separates In Progress from the other two. The remaining stages differ only by a shade a person would not notice, and are not part of this finding.

WHAT COULD NOT BE READ: Declined does not appear on any of the list's four views, so the colour the list would give it was not seen. The finding above does not depend on it.

EARLIER TODAY this result briefly said Declined had not been seen at all. That was wrong - Declined jobs do exist for this customer and sit lower in the search results than the first scan reached. The list above is the corrected, re-measured one.
